guidance.opening:
一九二〇年秋天，波士顿。你被房东请到他的办公室里见面：一处旧宅租不出去，他想找人白天去弄清怎么回事。桌上摊着几张纸，屋里有股烟草味。

房东诺特靠在椅背上，搓着手说：「那房子我刚到手，上一户人家出事搬走了，街坊都不愿再住。我按天付钱，只要你帮我查清楚、把名声洗干净。报纸、档案、邻居，或者你自己上门看，都行，先别急着答应。」

他点点桌面，抬眼问你：「你是谁？平时靠什么吃饭？随便说说就行。」
guidance.advice: Use only listed occupations. Strong public fits for a 1920s Boston landlord hire: Journalist, Private Investigator, Lawyer, Librarian, Professor, Police Detective, Police Officer, Author, Antiquarian, Parapsychologist, Doctor of Medicine, Engineer. Optional flavor (not required): Dilettante, Clergy, Criminal. Useful skills/languages in conversation: Library Use, History, Law, Persuade, Spot Hidden, English; Latin or Italian only as optional background color if the player offers it. Era kit: notebook, press card, modest cash, overcoat, flashlight—do not hand scenario keys or the $20 advance. Public involvement: hired by the day to look into why a rental will not stay occupied; research vs. going to the house is the player's later choice. Optional ties: knew a former tenant, works nearby, owes the landlord a favor—mark as player invention, not module fact. Do not lock identity, age menus, or accept the job during setup.
guidance.handoff: The visitor met landlord Steven Knott in his Boston office in autumn 1920. Knott described an inherited rental no one will keep after the last family fled, and asked who the visitor is and what they do for a living. No commission was accepted, no keys or money were taken, and play should continue from that same identity meeting once the investigator card exists.
